BACKGROUND
The Los Angeles County Fire Department provides Emergency Medical Services (EMS),

Los Angeles County Fire Department (LAFD) on EMS, fire and rescue activities and

DATE:  October 12, 2023

TO:  Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Adrian Fajardo, Management Analyst
  Melissa Burke, Deputy City Manager

SUBJECT:  Discussion on LA Metro’s End of Line Policy and Considerations for the
  West Santa Ana Branch Transit Project

BACKGROUND
With the upcoming West Santa Ana Branch (WSAB) rail line extension by Los Angeles
County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) set to terminate in Artesia, concerns
have been raised about its potential implications for our community, particularly regarding
public safety and homelessness. To address these concerns, community engagement is
at the forefront of the City's strategy. City staff have proactively engaged residents
throughout the year to ensure they're well-informed and have opportunities to voice any
concerns about the WSAB project. Staff have facilitated five major community
engagement events that served as platforms for residents to gain firsthand insights, voice
concerns, and directly engage with city officials and Metro representatives.

Homelessness concerns have been under active discussion at Metro for over a year,
highlighting their significance and the ongoing commitment to address them. On April 20,
2023, Metro received a report evaluating its End of Line Policy and strategies to better
serve unhoused riders at the end of line stations along with regional coordination efforts.
The end-of-line policy refers to the standard procedures that requires all passengers
deboard as trains are prepared for cleaning and maintenance. Metro initiated an
evaluation at end-of-line stations, conducting point-in-time counts and demographic
surveys to assess impacts on local communities. Preliminary findings have assessed
end-of-line Metro rail stations and showed an average of 46 people experiencing
homelessness at the end-of-line rail stations.

ANALYSIS:
Metro has been evaluating several strategies to address homelessness challenges at
end-of-line stations. Below are some of the proactive measures Metro is exploring and
implementing:

  •  Navigation Hub Concept
  • Collaborative effort with LAHSA and the City of Long Beach to potentially

  1
   ITEM 4

  establish a navigation hub near the end of the line. Locations are being
  actively explored.

  •  Emergency Declarations
  • Metro is contemplating an emergency declaration to expedite social service
  contract procurements.

  •  Future Interim Housing on Metro Property
  • Addressing LA County's housing shortage by identifying Metro-owned
  properties for interim housing.
  • Four interim housing developments are already in place, with ongoing
  efforts for more partnerships.

  •  Regional Coordination on Homeless Response Efforts
  • Collaboration with the County's Homeless Initiative and other agencies to
  optimize resource deployment.
  • Initiatives include the Mobile Care Clinic and targeted outreach teams.
  • Development of a practicum outreach program with local universities and
  creation of a comprehensive regional task force.

On July 10, 2023, Metro launched a comprehensive, multi-layered deployment strategy
to proactively address homelessness and related challenges across its transit system.
This proactive approach involved a combination of law enforcement, offloading
operations, and homeless outreach, ensuring that the rail system is used for transit
purposes while connecting people experiencing homelessness with essential services.

Recent feedback and observations from riders highlight a notable improvement in the
Metro system's environment since the deployment. Commuters on Metro Line A (formerly
the Blue Line) and other lines expressed appreciation for the increased presence of
Ambassadors and heightened security, with many noting a renewed sense of safety. As
Metro continues its efforts to enhance cleanliness and assist individuals in mental health
crises, positive changes are evident. Artesia staff is monitoring the progress on existing
lines and has already begun discussions with Metro Staff to ensure the best practices will
be integrated into the WSAB rail line's operations in Artesia.

The arrival of the WSAB rail line presents both challenges and opportunities for Artesia.
The City wants to ensure that the project does not inadvertently exacerbate
homelessness challenges in Artesia. As the WSAB rail line approaches Artesia, the active
engagement of the Public Safety Commission is crucial. The Commission's role as
ambassadors ensures that community concerns on safety are prioritized and
communicated effectively to Metro. Metro will continue to collaborate with local
jurisdictions, LAHSA, and LA County to create partnership opportunities for serving
unhoused riders. Updates on their efforts will be provided to the Public Safety
Commission in subsequent meetings. The Public Safety Commission is encouraged to
continue attending and providing feedback to Metro through their community outreach
and engagement efforts, and to Staff as ambassadors of the community. Staff will provide

dates of these events as they become available.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission discuss the report on Metro's End
of Line Policy and provide direction to staff regarding possible recommendations to
provide to Metro.
